title: Does this look fun?
author: Aromatic-Low-4578
selftext:
I built a battle simulator to try to push godot to its limits, which it turns out are pretty high. But it wasn't a game, so this what I've come up with so far. You are a god who bets on the outcomes of battles and then manipulates them with different effects to try to manipulate the outcome. Does this seem like a fun concept?

Built with: Godot (c#), Kenney assets for prototyping (Astra generated models shown here), Claude/Codex (Fable/Opus/Astra)

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
Hahaha I love the idea. That's a truly clever and novel idea.  I think the execution could be much more developed, more like what tuning environmental variables might really be like for a battle sandbox environment.

Makes me think of managing fish tanks or brewing.

comments.author: RepulsiveRaisin7
comments.body:
Hmm I'm skeptical. I've played many games of this style from Total War to Mechabellum. They have a few pillars, among them:

* Army composition
* Unit control and strategy
* Entertaining to watch

You have none of this. Only having a few abilities to drop rocks or thunder would be quite boring

Since (according to some) god made earth, I'd ground this in terrain manipulation. Ravines or gorges can block paths. Rivers can flood or dry up, giving one side an advantage. Mountains can be difficult to cross and cause losses. Volcanoes can erupt. Earthquakes or winds can cause trees to fall. Thunders could cause full on forest fires.

Create interesting maps where the army positioning is predetermined. The player's task is to solve the puzzle that allows their faction to win.

replies.author: Abject_Foot_4355
replies.body:
Although terrain manipulation would be a good add, i dont think the target audience is Total Wars heavy tactics players.

I suspect the target audience is more like Totally Accurate Battle Simulator. They just want chaos and cool physics.

I'd try it! I want to see soldiers flying.

comments.author: Ok_Effect_3214
comments.body: looks fun at glimpse. But can't tell what is going on tbh.

comments.author: bubbleofelephant
comments.body: Looks fun to me! Is there a demo?

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Not yet, I'll be sure to post here if I get that far though!

comments.author: IcyBother8850
comments.body:
Looks like it has potential but picking any side kinda ruins the immersion for me, why not make yourself a god for one of the nations and your quest is to aid them( Make it a campaign with increasingly harder odds for your side)( Maybe add some choices before each battle where you decide which unit you buff and what buff you give it).  
 Your army + You VS Enemies army + AI god or even a multiplayer mode where its you VS other player god? I see potential here :)

comments.author: Disposable110
comments.body:
Looks fun, but needs more gameplay mechanics like army building and a metagame with a reason to fight.

What were the main bottlenecks for you to get that many units on screen and the frame rate high? I got a citybuilder with some RTS mechanics in Godot and have been struggling with performance/optimisation despite getting rid of most of the Godot scripts and moving as much to the GPU as possible.
